source_name: Пари.мк / Вечер — известувања за членарини за картички и промени на тарифи
why_relevant: Mainstream business media occasionally publishes cross-bank card annual-fee tables (e.g. Sparkasse 1,500 MKD; CKB and TTK 1,200 MKD) and aggregate fee-income figures, which help benchmark tariff data against revenue reality.

source_name: Академски труд: „Провизии при трансакции со платежни картички“ (УГД Штип, Yearbook of Faculty of Law)
why_relevant: Academic decomposition of MK card transaction fee structure (merchant commission, cardholder fees, settlement fees) — gives the conceptual model for parsing acquiring price lists and identifies who bears which cost.

source_name: КИБС АД Скопје (Клириншка куќа КИБС) — corporate site
why_relevant: KIBS is the operator of the national retail (small-value) interbank clearing system and of the domestic instant-payments platform; it is owned by the commercial banks and is one of only two actors with transaction-level truth on domestic non-card payments. Site carries corporate news, instant-payment announcements, licences and regulatory PDFs.

source_name: НБРМ — КАСИС oversight page (central bank's page on CaSys)
why_relevant: The regulator's page on Интернационален картичен систем КаСис АД Скопје — the country's card switch/processor. Establishes CaSys's regulated status and role in the card payment system; the only official description of the card-clearing layer.

source_name: Македонска берза (MSE) — KIBS issuer page
why_relevant: KIBS is a joint-stock company with a securities symbol on the Macedonian Stock Exchange. The issuer page is the disclosure channel for shareholder structure (bank ownership), general-assembly materials and any audited financials — the way to get KIBS's economics without KIBS volunteering them.

source_name: CompanyWall / ABV.mk business directories — КИБС АД Скопје and КаСис АД profiles
why_relevant: Commercial aggregators that resurface Central Registry financials (revenue, headcount, blocked-account status) for free or cheaply, giving a fast first read on operator scale and year-on-year trend before paying for official filings.

source_name: Македонска банкарска асоцијација (МБА) — Е-Билтен and KIBS tag
why_relevant: The banking association's e-bulletin is where KIBS and the banks explain infrastructure projects to their own peers — cost-benefit analyses for instant payments, regional benchmarking, membership news. KIBS was admitted as a full MBA member, and the site maintains a dedicated КИБС tag feed. Higher signal density than press releases.

source_name: Diners Club Macedonia — diners.mk / my.diners.com.mk
why_relevant: Local Diners Club licensee, operating since 1996 as the country's first credit/charge card and now 30 years in market. As a three-party-scheme licensee outside the Visa/Mastercard rails it is a distinct acceptance network with its own merchant base and instalment programmes; its merchant/partner listings reveal acceptance footprint.

source_name: Mastercard Europe Newsroom — press releases (North Macedonia filter)
why_relevant: Scheme-side announcements naming North Macedonia — e.g. the National Digital Identity Service launched with the government and NLB Banka Skopje (Nov 2021). Schemes benefit from announcing wins, so this is where partnership, product and occasional growth-percentage claims surface first.

source_name: Visa Inc. investor/press site — visa.gcs-web.com
why_relevant: Visa's press and investor disclosures carry CEE-level product pushes (Tap to Phone, contactless penetration) that frame what is being sold into MK. Country-level MK data is rarely broken out, so treat as context and product-roadmap signal rather than as an MK statistics source.

source_name: mk.wikipedia — Платен промет / Македонски Интербанкарски Платен Систем
why_relevant: Not a statistics source, but an efficient glossary and actor-map bootstrap in Macedonian: correct official names, the МИПС/КИБС division of labour (MIPS for large-value and above-1-million-denar or real-time payments; KIBS for retail), and outbound citations to NBRM primary pages.

source_name: ProCredit Bank MK blog — 'КИБС или МИПС плаќање — која е разликата?'
why_relevant: Bank-published explainer that reveals operational parameters of the two systems as banks actually apply them (thresholds, cut-offs, fee logic, ownership by 15 banks). Bank explainer pages across all MK banks are a cheap, comparable way to reverse-engineer clearing rules and pricing without operator cooperation.

source_name: Министерство за европски прашања — SEPA accession announcements
why_relevant: Official government record of North Macedonia's SEPA accession (accepted by the European Payments Council as the 39th SEPA member; PSP operational readiness Oct 2025, effective 7 Oct 2025). SEPA access reshapes euro clearing routing and is the key structural change in this cell's infrastructure layer.

source_name: НБРСМ — Платни системи и платежни услуги (payment systems & services hub, incl. registers of payment institutions and payment system operators)
why_relevant: Hub page from which the PI register, EMI register, payment-system-operator register, regulation and payment statistics branch. Single best snowball root for the whole non-bank payments licensing landscape.

source_name: НБРСМ — Прашања и одговори за крипто-средствата (crypto-assets Q&A / supervisory position)
why_relevant: Central bank's stated position on crypto-assets and crypto-adjacent payment services in MK — defines the legal perimeter for crypto payment apps and exchange operators, which currently operate without a dedicated licence.

source_name: Paysera Македонија (first domestic e-money institution licensed by NBRSM)
why_relevant: Reported as the first EMI licensed to a domestic entity by NBRSM (2025). Its product pages, pricing and news are the primary read on wallet/IBAN/e-money adoption outside banks. NOTE: the .mk domain is my inference of the corporate site and is unverified.

source_name: Iute Pay DOOEL Skopje / iute.mk (EMI licensee, BNPL and MyIute wallet)
why_relevant: Iute Pay received an EMI licence from NBRSM (July 2025); Iute MK is also the largest BNPL operator in the country (reported 650+ partners, ~1,000 sales points, ~100 e-shops, 50k+ BNPL buyers). Company site + newsroom is the richest single non-bank product/partnership feed in the cell.

source_name: Iute Group investor relations / regulatory disclosures (Nasdaq Tallinn & Frankfurt-listed parent)
why_relevant: Listed parent of Iute Pay MK must disclose audited segment data — MK loan/BNPL/payment volumes, customer counts, wallet adoption. Rare case where a non-bank MK payments player's numbers are subject to securities-disclosure discipline.

source_name: Унија Финансиска Скопје (UFS) — non-bank Western Union master agent network
why_relevant: Largest non-bank remittance payout network in MK: reported 250+ agency locations across 30+ towns as a Western Union agent. Directly evidences cash-out footprint and remittance corridor capacity outside the banking channel — the core of this cell.

source_name: Western Union / MoneyGram / Ria agent pages of MK banks (Halkbank, Komercijalna, Stopanska, Sparkasse, TTK)
why_relevant: Bank pages disclose which global MTO each institution is agent for, the number of payout points (e.g. Halkbank as WU agent across 38 branches; TTK as MoneyGram agent), currencies and fee schedules — a cheap way to map the MTO-to-distributor matrix and pricing without paying for it.

source_name: Асоцијација за е-трговија на Македонија (AETM) — analysis & reports
why_relevant: Publishes recurring quantified e-commerce/online-payment analyses for MK (quarterly transaction value and count, domestic vs cross-border split, new online sales points, Western Balkans regional report), largely built on NBRSM data but with breakdowns the NBRSM does not publish. Also a convening body linking PSPs, banks and merchants.

source_name: Monri Payments (Payten/Asseco SEE) — regional gateway operating in North Macedonia
why_relevant: Cross-border PSP gateway explicitly serving the MK market (WebPay, instalment payments, tokenisation) and part of the Payten/Asseco group. Its MK site and merchant/product pages show what acceptance capabilities are available to MK e-merchants outside the CaSys/bank duopoly.

source_name: eCommerce4all.mk — e-payment / online transaction processing knowledge base
why_relevant: Practitioner-oriented guide enumerating which processors, gateways and banks an MK merchant can actually contract with, and the onboarding steps. Useful pointer for discovering smaller PSPs and acquirer arrangements not visible in regulator lists.

source_name: IT.mk — Macedonian tech/fintech news outlet
why_relevant: Covers fintech licensing, wallet launches and PSP partnerships in Macedonian earlier and in more detail than English sources (e.g. reported Paysera's e-money approval). Good early-warning feed for new non-bank entrants.

source_name: Bloomberg Adria (MK) — crypto & fintech market coverage
why_relevant: Business-grade regional outlet reporting on the crypto-exchange grey zone in MK ('crypto exchanges operate legally but no licences exist yet') and on fintech entrants. Higher editorial standard than most local outlets.

source_name: World Bank / KNOMAD remittance data for North Macedonia
why_relevant: Comparable, machine-readable remittance inflow series (personal remittances received, % of GDP — ~2.7% for MK in 2024) plus KNOMAD corridor-cost briefs. Provides the sizing baseline for the remittance-agent segment and international benchmarking.

source_name: Faktor.mk / Meta.mk / MKD.mk / off.net.mk — MK general business press on e-money and payment licensing
why_relevant: General-news layer that reports NBRSM secondary-legislation adoption and individual licence grants, often the fastest public signal that a new non-bank payment actor exists. Useful for building the actor timeline before registers update.

source_name: Закон за платежни услуги и платни системи — consolidated text (NBRSM PDF)
why_relevant: Primary law defining PI/EMI categories, agent and distributor rules, safeguarding of client funds, and the reporting obligations that generate all downstream non-bank payment statistics. Anchor document for interpreting every other source in the cell.
